name: Spastic

tenures.source: promotions/wia/archive/superstars-2003-01.html (the fed’s own roster page, Wayback-captured 24 January 2003)
tenures.note: Ranked #6 in the January 2003 rankings (promotions/wia/archive/rankings-2003-01.html (the fed’s own weekly rankings, Wayback-captured 24 January 2003)): “had a tough break on Insanity but that didn’t cause him to slack off... the staff felt he needed to be in the World Title Tourny... he’s a real character and could lead WIA.” On 26 January 2003 the fed’s own founder handed the promotion to him outright. The announcement, bylined by Spastic himself as “The New Owner,” says he “will now be known by his real name” and that things continue as normal, the pay-per-view pushed back a week (promotions/wia/archive/news-2003-01-26.html (the fed’s own news/front page, Wayback-captured 26 March 2003; its own dateline reads 26 January 2003)). Dropped out of the fed’s own later Top 10 sidebar in the same document, consistent with having moved from roster to ownership.

notes: “Spastic” became WIA’s own real-world site owner on 26 January 2003. The fed’s own announcement blends the wrestler’s ring name and the handler’s out-of-fiction ownership role in one document.
caption: Ranked sixth on his own roster in January 2003, “a real character,” and by the end of that same month the new owner of the whole promotion.
